title: Tenant tail spikes from prefetch eviction during large-embedding fanouts — emergency patch & plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Production incident: a single enterprise tenant observed sustained TTFT spikes (first-token latency increases of 2.5-4x and tokens/sec drop of ~60%) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments during large-embedding fanout workloads. Root cause (investigation summary): interaction between aggressive prefix prefetch eviction logic in the KV cache and high-concurrency embedding fanouts caused repeated eviction-repopulate thrash. This was amplified when mixed-int8 quantized model variants were selected by the kernel autoselector, which slightly increased per-token compute and widened the effective queuing window, making eviction more likely. Customer workload characteristics: many thousands of short concurrent embedding requests with high fanout to reranking/score models, dominated by repeating prefixes that should have been sticky but got evicted under current heuristics.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:14 - Alert: PagerDuty fired (PD# 2026-03012-01). Support case TKT-2026-349 opened by AE Alice Monroe on behalf of customer ‘DataScale’. Initial symptom: intermittent 4x TTFT for embedding-backed endpoints.

2026-03-12 09:40 - Triage call with oncall, infra, and runtime teams. Observed strong correlation between embedding fanout rate and KV eviction counters. Hypothesis formed: aggressive global cache quota + LRU eviction under concurrency leads to hot-prefix eviction.

2026-03-12 11:05 - Emergency mitigation deployed (canary): temporary bypass of soft-eviction for keys with >N hits in last M seconds (config flag runtime.kv.soft_evict_threshold disabled for canary hosts). Canary rollout at 5% on Hosted and 10% on Dedicated (region-us-west1). Early telemetry: first-token latency for canary reduced by ~45% for affected tenant.
2026-03-12 14:30 - Customer update: In-Flight mitigation applied; asking for ETA on global fix. Solutions Eng (Priya Rao) helped validate rollout impact on customer staging.

2026-03-12 16:00 - Observation: disabling soft-eviction reduced TTFT but increased steady-state memory pressure on some Dedicated hosts. Decided to pair soft-eviction bypass with an adaptive cache ceiling per-tenant to avoid OOM; spike memory alerts tuned to avoid noisy reboots.

2026-03-13 08:20 - Hotfix PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/10422 - implements (A) eviction pin for hot-prefixes, (B) short-lived token-bucket rate limiter for embedding fanouts when per-tenant concurrency > X, (C) conservative kernel fallback for quantized variants under high eviction churn. Review requested from @samantha-ops and @diego-kernel.
2026-03-13 12:45 - Security review: no customer data exfiltration risk; change only affects ephemeral cache behavior. Marked security_review_required=false. Sec team gave ack at 2026-03-13 13:05.

2026-03-13 15:00 - Canary rollout v1.0 (PR#10422) promoted to 25% across Hosted and Dedicated; Private installer built for customer-specific deployment and customer agreed to coordinate. Telemetry: avg TTFT dropped to pre-incident baseline for the tenant; tokens/sec recovered to ~90% baseline.

2026-03-14 10:10 - Edge case found during canary: under extremely bursty fanout, pinned-prefix approach delayed eviction of cold keys causing a small increase in tail GC pauses on two Dedicated hosts (observed ~30s heap compaction). Decided to tune pin TTL to 60s and add a soft-shedder that temporarily rejects non-critical background requests when heap pressure > 75%.

2026-03-14 16:50 - Rollout plan updated: staggered promotion with region pacing, automated health checks (SLO: median TTFT < 200ms, p95 < 700ms), and an automatic rollback if OOM or GC pause rate increases beyond threshold. Runtime release target: runtime-1.22. Patch will be feature-flagged for Private installs.
2026-03-15 09:00 - Customer comms drafted (Confluence doc) and sent to Account SLA owner for approval. Postmortem kickoff scheduled for 2026-03-21. Follow-ups assigned for long-term improvements.
notes: Next steps: implement adaptive per-tenant cache quota algorithm (owner: Marco), add unit+e2e tests that simulate high fanout embeddings (owner: runtime team), and add a dashboard for eviction churn per tenant (owner: observability).
Coordinate Dedicated maintenance window for final rollout and ensure Private customers receive feature-flagged patch and migration guide.
Postmortem should document telemetry thresholds that triggered mitigation, and include cost trade-off analysis for pinned hot-prefixes vs eviction aggressiveness.
